key_insight: PINNs reproduce the global evolution of multidimensional turbulent, self-gravitating gas while showing weak training-cost dependence on spatial resolution.
engineering_relevance: This mesh-free approach offers a potential complement to grid-based solvers for computationally demanding compressible, self-gravitating flows.
method: Embed governing equations for isothermal, self-gravitating gas in the neural-network training objective.
Model subsonic and supersonic turbulent evolution in two and three dimensions.
Benchmark predicted density and velocity fields against the finite-volume code Athena++.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate global evolution over multiple free-fall times across turbulent realizations, Mach numbers, and dimensionalities, with training cost increasing by less than 25% from 128³ to 1024³.
watch_item: Global agreement does not establish accuracy for localized shocks or collapsing structures; these require targeted error and conservation checks.
paper_title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
